## 20 Oct 2026: the game code split: the start fetches only the code it runs

(owner, 20 Oct 2026, told "the download at the start is still about 1.5 MB, and most of that is the game code in one piece (2.25 MB,
845 KB gzipped). Splitting it up is a bigger change to how the page is built": "Yes fix game code")
- **How** (`tools/chunks.cjs`, `tools/chunkscope.cjs`, `build.py`, `tools/bundle.cjs`): a function whose body starts with `'@name';` is cut
  out of the page at build time into chunk `name`. On the website each chunk is its own file, `x-name.<hash>.js` (cached for good like the
  rest of `/g/`), fetched by `await LOAD('name')`; in `dist/market.html` the chunks stay in the page and `LOAD` is instant, so every test
  of the single page runs the same cut code. The page keeps a small stand-in for each cut function: on its first call it makes the real
  one with every name around it as before (names that never change are handed in; the ones that do are read and written live), so the
  source reads exactly as it did. A cut function that runs before its chunk came still works (the chunk is fetched there and then and the
  page waits) and the console says `chunk name was not loaded before use (#n)`; `dist/chunks.txt` lists every cut function by number.
  Without `acorn` (a local build with no `npm ci`) every chunk simply stays in the page.
- **Places, fetched on the way in, behind their black fades**: `dungeon` (the levels' builder, the slimes and skeleton fighters, the
  skeletons), `park` (the fountain and lake, the brook, the pond, the cave, the rocks and lamps), `dojo` (the hall and the ninja), `fire`
  (your fire escape), `club`, `arcade`, `vcr` (VCR repair), `bath` (the bath house's inside). The ways in wait for them: the dungeon's
  door, `PARK.load`, `STORE.offGo`/`enter`/`ensure`/`offAt`, the rooms' swap, the menu's places (`UI.goPlace` now waits) and a saved
  spot (the restore waits for the later chunk first). The dungeon's slimes and fighters are made the first time you go down (the slime
  bottles' names and prices are still known from the start).
- **Later**: every other function the start never runs, ~650 of them (~540 KB of source: the store's rooms and their makers, menus and
  panels, editors, mail, the feel lab...), fetched as soon as the start is done; the store's background rooms wait for it. They are
  marked by `tools/later.cjs` from what the start runs in Chromium (a new player's start with a few seconds of keys, mouse, the views and
  the menu, a walk to Market St, then a returning player's start; anything that calls `LOAD` stays in the start file). New code stays in
  the start file until the tool is run again.
- **Dead code out**: 40 functions and constants nothing used (the old street-scene helpers `box`/`cyl`/`plane`/`worldUV`, `bush`,
  `laundryTile`, the dojo hall's `djWallCol`/`djOpen`/`djIvy`, the guitar's and piano's unused chains, the octopus's `octPic`, the stalls'
  `table`/`basket`, the bodega's third-floor lot...), and five 256-pixel textures (grass, asphalt, concrete, earth, wood) painted at every start and never used.
- **Measured** (CI, the website under `wrangler dev`, gzipped, everything fetched before the first frame): the start's download about
  1,513 KB to 1,307 KB; the game code 840 KB to 607 KB (2.23 MB to 1.66 MB unzipped); three.js, the rig and the data as before. Right
  after the first frame the later chunk, 190 KB; going in: park 18 KB, dungeon 12 KB (plus its skeletons' data as before), arcade 12 KB,
  club 6 KB, VCR repair 6 KB, fire escape 4 KB, dojo 3 KB, bath house 2 KB. First frame about the same here (four runs: 10.5/9.6,
  23.0/24.2, 18.9/20.3, 12.1/11.6 s against main; under software graphics the building dominates and the files come from the same
  machine): the gain is the download on a real connection. The budget check: the same triangles, draws and lights at the start and in
  the park; its frame medians swing both ways between runs (3-4 frames sampled in the park), the systems' own time a frame no higher.
- **Checked**: `tests/places.cjs` (now in the site workflow) logs in on the real worker, checks the start fetches no chunk, enters every
  place (each fetches its file, builds, no page errors, no late fetch), then reloads with a saved spot inside the dungeon; all pass, the
  site check too.

- **The three new characters cut to about 4,000 triangles each** (owner, 20 Oct 2026: "these are for a low res pixel game, do they really
  need to be so big?"; his pick "4000", as 19 Oct's cut of the heaviest pawns): their curves are sampled more coarsely (fewer rings and
  segments on every lathe, tube and surface; the same profiles, proportions, bones, cloth and motion). THE MANATEE 11,876 → 3,748;
  THE RAIN FISH 11,236 → 3,764 with the hood; NUMBER 80 14,324 → 4,048 (his horn four rings, not seven).

## 21 Oct 2026: a stale open tab auto-refreshes when a place's code is gone

The owner, playing the live site: "bath house isnt loading", with the console 404ing `/g/x-bath.<hash>.js` and a wall of
uncaught `bath 404`. THE MARKET is one long-lived page: the shell loads `m.<hash>.js`, and that running code fetches each
place's chunk on demand (`x-name.<hash>.js`). Every deploy content-hashes the files, so a new deploy gives new names and the
worker (`worker/door.js`) 404s anything not in the current deploy. A tab left open from before a redeploy keeps running the old
`m.js`, which asks for a chunk by a hash the new deploy replaced — so entering that place 404s and it never builds. (The chunk
itself is fine: `tests/places.cjs` enters the bath house on every push.) `136-version.js`'s `peek()` already shows A NEW VERSION
IS READY, but only every 90s and on your action, so a deploy landing just before you walk in slips through.

A failed chunk fetch is proof the page is stale, so the loader now acts on it (owner chose auto-refresh over the notice): a
404/403 on a chunk saves the spot and reloads once (`__CLOAD`/`__CSYNC` in `build.py`); position is restored on reload
(`135-where.js`), so you land back where you were on the current build and the place opens. A one-shot guard makes later loads
wait rather than storm the network before the reload navigates, and `swap()` (`130-rooms.js`) now catches the rejection, so no
console spam and no wedged entry. The 90s peek stays for the proactive case. (Only the website runtime; the single-file
`dist/market.html` keeps its chunks in the page and never fetches.)

## 21 Oct 2026: butterflies wait for the later chunk (main's build-check green again)

The site's build-check had been red since the new-layout steps (#164–#168): `tests/places.cjs` failed on a returning player whose saved spot is down in the dungeon, with `chunk later was not loaded before use (#269)`. #269 is `BF.add` (`056-butterflies.js`), the butterfly model maker, which lives in the `later` chunk. Butterflies spawn on the lawn and flowerbed chunks as they build around you (`143-bfly.js`); on a saved-dungeon start the surface still builds, so `BF.add` was reached before `later` had come, forcing the synchronous fetch the test forbids. The park's inside (#167) widened where butterflies spawn; `tools/later.cjs` (which only un-marks what runs in its fresh / Market St / park-gate scenarios, not a saved-dungeon start) was not re-run, so `BF.add` stayed in `later`.

Fix (`143-bfly.js`): hold all butterfly spawning — the `WEEDS.onAdd` hook, the first sweep of existing chunks, and the once-a-second turn/weather loop — until the start is up (`window.__started`) and `await LOAD('later')` has resolved. Butterflies belong in `later` (the first frame never needs them), so this keeps them out of the start download and off the saved-spot start's critical path; waiting for `__started` first means the butterflies ride the start's own `LOAD('later')` (fired after the first frame in `163-main-15.js`) instead of pulling the chunk in early, so "no chunk at the start" still holds. Checked: `tests/places.cjs` — every place builds, the saved-dungeon start has no slow fetch, "all good".
## 21 Oct 2026: the Walker's arm-clearance search cached while still

- A profile of the rig (`src/001-rig.js`, lifted from the built page as `tests/footworld.cjs` lifts it) found `pose()` was the whole
  per-frame cost (step ~0.05 ms; pose 0.41-0.74 ms a character), and almost all of pose was `clearArms`: a binary search that builds the
  pose up to ~13 times a frame to swing each arm clear of the body. A still Walker's answer never changes, yet it was recomputed every
  frame (and standing cost *more* than walking, 0.67 vs 0.41 ms, because at rest the arms hang near the body so the full search fires) —
  against the owner's "things at rest stay still". Now `clearArms` caches its result keyed on everything `walkPose` reads for the arms,
  and engages the cache only when fully still (`st.w===0`), where the pose is phase-independent, so the key holds frame to frame; while
  moving it takes the old path untouched. The one side effect the skipped probes used to have — advancing `walkPose`'s nod-smoothing filter
  `st.ndS` (~14x a frame) — is replayed exactly on a cache hit (the nod target is 0 while still, so the decay is `*0.94` per skipped probe);
  `st.pyS` is provably constant while still (feet are phase-independent when `w==0`), so it needs no replay. Measured against the unpatched
  rig over stand / walk / run / circle / turns / stop / start: **0 joint difference and 0 differing pixels** (300 rendered frames, the stop
  transient included) — output is bit-identical. Cost: standing ~7x cheaper a frame (0.73 -> 0.10 ms, 86% less); walking and running
  unchanged (within noise). This matters per visible character, so it scales with the street's Walkers.

The SYS bus already isolates its handlers; added SYS.go(fn,name) (same warn-once) and routed every per-frame system call through it (075-main-13), so a throwing system warns once and the frame still renders. SYS.run entries, assignments and the render call itself unchanged.

## 24 Oct 2026: fight fixes (release 1 of 5)
Owner: "look at the overall game mechanices for fighting, pvm, pvp, look for errors or things not funished", then "Yes, fix all of them", "Mash to break free", "Faint first, die if hit again". At no health you faint (out cold about 15 s, the medic comes, up again with some health); a real blow while you are out cold kills you; drowning still kills. Held down or carried, mash any key to break free; a blow while you are down doesn't keep you down longer. Ghosts can't fight, trip or be grabbed and others walk through them. Blocking softens a player's shove and stops their knockdown. Fire and other blows with no direction can't be blocked or parried.
Rule: only the one holding you can throw you; the server passes a blow, grab or throw only between players close together on the same level and in the same room.

## 24 Oct 2026: martial arts and stamina (release 2 of 5)
Owner chose "Martial arts + stamina". MARTIAL ARTS is a skill (in the skills list, starts at 10): bare-hand blows that land and kills train it, and it makes your punches and kicks stronger. A punch costs a little stamina, a kick more; with almost none left your blows land weak. At no stamina you can't run until a third is back.

## 24 Oct 2026: bare-hand block and more moves (release 3 of 5)
Owner chose "Bare-hand block + more moves on keys". P blocks with bare hands too (the arms come up; it softens a blow, more with MARTIAL ARTS; only a sword parries). New keys: N slap, I crouch (hold; then J an uppercut, K a sweep), 2 leg sweep, 3 back flip, 4 front flip; all rebindable, and others see them. The stale T "ghost's guitar" line is gone from the controls.

## 24 Oct 2026: hit feedback and others' health (release 4 of 5)
Owner chose "Hit feedback + health of others". When your blow lands on a player they flash and you hear it. A creature's blow jolts you back a step and you flinch. A hurt player shows a health bar under their name; a dead player is a pale see-through ghost named "(GHOST)". Stamina comes back only after a short rest from running, punching or swinging.

Inside, every good carries its real name on its label (Café Bustelo, El Pico, Goya rice, beans, Adobo and Sazón, Wonder, Cheerios, Corn Flakes, Campbell's, Chef Boyardee, Ronzoni, Vienna sausage, Spam, Wise, Cheez Doodles, Drake's, Entenmann's, Hershey's, Now & Later, Bazooka, Chick-O-Stick, Coca-Cola, Pepsi, Sprite, Schaefer, Colt 45, Miller High Life, Malta Goya, Coco Rico, Yoo-hoo-era sodas, Dairylea, Tuscan, Dannon, Tide, Ajax, Clorox, Pampers, Kool-Aid, the 7-day candles, Carolina rice sacks on the floor, platanos), a middle shelf unit and two window displays. Rule: the bodega's goods are real 1980s New York products, named; nothing invented.
## 1 Nov 2026: 480 lines under the PS2 filter
Owner, of the review's first item (the frame shaded at the screen's own pixels, then box-filtered into 240 lines): "lets do this first". While the PS2 filter is on the picture is drawn at 480 lines at most (each of its 240 cells reads a 2x2 box, so the picture is the same for a fraction of the pixels); HIGH and HIGHEST mean 480 then. With the filter off the RESOLUTION steps are as before. Rule: nothing drawn finer than the look can show.

- 1 Nov 2026, THE CATACOMB RUN is now an off-world jungle auto-runner (owner: "the catacomb run should be in the middle of the jungle and you should be running fast, jump, rolling, ducking, dodging, etc. for as long as you can", and the holodeck adventures "shouldnt stay in holodeck ... take you to a new off world map", Temple-Run style): RUN fades you off the map to a jungle track (`ROOMS.off.catrun`); you auto-run, speeding up, and the arrows jump the logs, crouch under the branches and switch lane past the rocks; a hit wipes you out, your furthest metres kept as a best, then fades you back into the holodeck. The slimes and waves are gone from the run (the dungeon keeps its slimes). Rule: each holodeck adventure is its own off-world map, entered on RUN and dropped on exit.

## 2 Nov 2026: ROAM — a ship among the meteors, the holodeck's VR flight
Owner: "i want to work on a VR game for TSFM where you are in a cockpit of a small ship in space flying around meteors, super realistic graphics and textures of interior POV of ship, real controls and be able to go in full 360 rotation when flying"; his picks: "holodeck", "free flight for now, boost, shoot lasers, missiles, blow up meteors (smaller ones, big one you can blow up parts of it at a time)", the flight model mine (arcade with a flight assist), "using vr controllers quest", "fixed cockpit", on screen too ("yes"), "solo", free assets, named "ROAM". ROAM is a free holodeck program (`146bc-roam.js`, its own chunk, `tests/roam.cjs`): a realistic cockpit (stick, throttle and screens that move and read live; steel, paint, leather and glass painted in code — Poly Haven was not reachable from the workspace, so nothing is downloaded) fixed round you, full 360° flight, boost, lasers that break rocks and missiles that break big ones a piece at a time, a hull that wears on ramming and sends you back to the holodeck when gone. On screen the mouse or the arrows aim, W/S throttle, A/D roll, Shift boost, Space lasers, F missile, hold Q to end; in the headset the Quest sticks fly (left throttle and roll, right pitch and yaw, A boost, triggers lasers and missile, hold Y to end). Rule: a vehicle you sit in owns the controls and the camera through `SHARED.drive`; the frame, the headset and the gamepad read it, nothing else.
- Owner: "remove quiet island from game". The `island/` page (19 Oct 2026, its own page, never part of THE MARKET) is gone; it was the only thing of its kind left.
- 2 Nov 2026, owner: "use gritty realistic shapes and graphics, atmospheric, dark, lights, glow, etc. go all out, controls make sense. hand tracking. realistic textures like the subway platform". ROAM's cockpit is painted pixel by pixel like the platform (scuffed gunmetal panels with rivets, rust and grime, chipped matte dash with stencils, brushed scratched steel, cracked leather, diamond-plate floor, smeared glass), dark and lit by its own instruments (amber and cyan glow, LED strips, a red warning light), with thruster puffs when you steer, a flare off the sun, dust motes streaming past, nebulae, a floating lucky charm, cracks across the glass as the hull goes, a flight card on the dash for the controls in use. Hand tracking: take the stick with your right hand (lean it, twist to yaw, pinch to fire), the throttle with your left (push past the stop to boost, pinch for a missile), hold the red button to end; controllers can grip them the same way.
- 2 Nov 2026, owner: "this game should not have the same haze effect or be using same graphics as the main game, needs to be its own thing, should look realism". ROAM draws its own scene and picture: none of the game's world, lights, haze or passes reach it; filmic tone mapping, a little bloom on screen, the headset drawn straight. Rule: a vehicle's own world (`SHARED.drive.scene`, `.draw`) is drawn in place of the game's while you sit in it.
- 2 Nov 2026, owner: "screens should be centered focused towards you, not all flat, small intimate cockpit, dark, retrotech"; "doesnt look like cockpit window or controls overhead at all"; "way too bright". ROAM's cockpit is a small framed canopy of flat panes across the whole width (no dome), three screens wrapped round the seat (an amber CRT in the middle, green either side), round dials, an overhead console of switches, warning cells and breakers, side consoles with the throttle, the stick, the guarded red END button, a keypad and working switches (CABIN LIGHTS, SIGHT, RADAR RANGE; touch them or L, H, N), the maker's plate, a taped note and a tally on the bulkhead. Lit dim: the screens and a few small lamps.

## 2 Nov 2026: the Mall's elms over the entrance walk; the lake's track, rail and cherry; tufts at the trees' feet
Owner (his picture of the Mall in Central Park): "I want to make the trees this large compared to avatars and shaped exactly the same, make the entrance full of trees that go over like this". The park's trees are elms now, 26 to 31 m: a bare trunk forking into leaders that climb and arch out, the crown an umbrella wider than the tree is tall; the walk from the main gate to the plaza is lined on both sides with two staggered rows of them, their crowns meeting over it. The edge ring and the rows past the north wall stay as they were. In the isometric view the leaves over you open fully round you.
Owner (his picture of the reservoir's running path): "add a super large cherry blossom tree by the lake, add this rail around the lake. you should be able to jog around it. very atmospheric. calm, real water, clear, like hudson same options. real fish, etc." The big lake has a running track the length of its shore inside the park (planked where the brook leaves the lake), lamps beside it, and an iron rail on its water side, open where a path meets the water and at three gates for swimmers; a cherry twice as wide as it is tall leans out over the track and the water at the lake's end nearest the plaza; the shore's trees stand past the track. The lake's water is the Hudson's, calm, seen through by depth; the river's panel (a double click on either water) sets both. ## 2 Nov 2026: THE CATACOMB RUN in VR, and how a run starts
Owner: "lets work on the catacomb run game in VR, logically, should start out in rear view, test all the controls, think of how the game should start in order for players to have a chance at playing, winning, learning, knowing". The run is seen from behind the runner (in the headset too, turning held so the track stays ahead; your own VR view back after). You start standing at the line with the controls shown in your device's words (keyboard, pad or Quest), free to try them, then 3, 2, 1, GO (your best shown). The first three obstacles teach one each (a log to jump, a branch to duck, a rock to dodge), far apart, each named as it nears, a miss forgiven; then NOW RUN, and it speeds up. Every 100 m is called, passing your best too; a wipeout says your best. Controls: left/right (A/D, the stick) lanes, up (W, the stick, A, space) jumps, down held (S, the stick) ducks, roll (Y, the left trigger) ducks too. In the headset every message shows on its card, and a door or fade no longer snaps you back to where your head was. Rule: a place that needs a view in the headset asks for it (`VR.ask`) and gives it back.

## 4 Nov 2026: THE STRANGEST FAIR
Owner: "lets build out an amusement park, rollercoasters, rides, etc."; of the sites: "lets put it on the left side of map in the green area behind all the buildings but lets make it concrete"; "lets add every single feature you said, and move all the other stuff we have there or on the same street (like the arcade, theater, playhouse, etc) should all be on that road"; "use the characters we have in game already from polyfork to work at all the places needed".
- THE STRANGEST FAIR (`fair` in data/world.json): a concrete lot behind the West St row, fenced, its gate on West St between the movie theatre and the museum, a ticket booth inside the gate (a strip of five for $8), lamps lit after dark. Rides: the Ferris wheel, carousel, swing ride, pirate ship, teacups, scrambler, drop tower, slingshot, roller coaster, log flume, haunted ride, miniature railway, sky ride; the kart track with rental karts (laps timed, your best kept, the fair's record shared) and the bumper cars. The midway: ring toss, milk bottles, balloon darts, high striker, shooting gallery, skee-ball, whack-a-mole, duck pond, basketball toss, water-gun race, claw machine, coin pusher; prize tickets traded at the prize counter (kazoo, pennant, plush, giant plush); food stalls (cotton candy, popcorn, lemonade, corn dogs, funnel cake, eaten from the pack); the arcade tent with the six cabinet games; the stage (shows 14:00 to 21:00) and fireworks at 21:00; the photo booth and ride photos on the coaster and the flume; the fortune teller; the map board; the funhouse (wavy floor, the barrel, the slide). A new skill, MIDWAY GAMES.
- The movie theatre moved to West St (its builder turned onto its faced lot like the bar's); the arcade, the playhouse and the theatre are all on West St with the fair's gate.
- The fair's staff are polyfork characters with jobs at its posts: the townspeople with no job and the themed visitors (held for sections B to H) run the gate, the rides, the booths, the stalls, the tent and the stage until their own sections exist (docs/CAST.md).
- Rules: anything you ride at the fair is one mechanic (`FAIR.ride`: run from the shared clock so everyone sees the same ride, seats boarded where they stand, a ticket a ride); a game booth is one mechanic (`MIDWAY`: a timing throw or a reaction round, prize tickets by how well you do); a job at a place names its post (`job.spot`, the place registers its posts with `CREW.spots`); a place in the level file may name its door (`door`); nothing grows through concrete. Still to come: other players' karts and bumper cars bump only in looks (no shared physics); the sky ride never stops, board a low chair at either station.
